Class ListElement<T>

java.lang.Object
dev.tamboui.toolkit.element.StyledElement<ListElement<T>>
dev.tamboui.toolkit.elements.ListElement<T>
Type Parameters:
T - the type of data items backing each list entry
All Implemented Interfaces:
Styleable, Element
public final class ListElement<T> extends StyledElement<ListElement<T>>
A scrollable container that displays a list of selectable items.

Unlike ListWidget (which only displays text), ListElement can display any StyledElement as list items, including complex layouts like rows with multiple styled children.

Example usage: 

list("Item 1", "Item 2", "Item 3")
    .state(listState)
    .highlightColor(Color.YELLOW)
    .title("My List")
    .rounded()

// With complex items:
list(
    row(text("Name: ").bold(), text("John").green()),
    row(text("Age: ").bold(), text("25").cyan())
).state(listState)

CSS selectors:

  • ListElement - styles the container (border, background)
  • ListElement-item - styles each list item
  • ListElement-item:selected - styles the selected item
  • ListElement-item:nth-child(odd/even) - zebra striping
  • ListElement-scrollbar-thumb - styles the scrollbar thumb
  • ListElement-scrollbar-track - styles the scrollbar track
See Also:
  • for simple text-only lists at the widget level

    • scrollToEnd

      public ListElement<T> scrollToEnd()
      Scrolls the list to show the last items.

      Unlike autoScroll(), this scrolls to the end immediately without requiring a selection. Useful for chat messages, logs, or other content where you want to always show the most recent items.

      Note: This always forces scroll to end, overriding any user scrolling. For logs or chat where you want auto-scroll that pauses when the user scrolls up, use stickyScroll() instead.

      Note: Cannot be combined with autoScroll() or stickyScroll().

      Returns:
      this element
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if another scroll mode is already enabled

    • stickyScroll

      public ListElement<T> stickyScroll()
      Enables sticky scroll behavior for the list.

      With sticky scroll, the list automatically scrolls to show new items at the bottom, but pauses auto-scrolling when the user scrolls up. Auto-scrolling resumes when the user scrolls back to the bottom.

      This is ideal for logs, chat messages, or activity feeds where you want to show the latest content but allow users to scroll back through history.

      Note: Cannot be combined with autoScroll() or scrollToEnd().

      Returns:
      this element
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if another scroll mode is already enabled

    • preferredSize

      public Size preferredSize(int availableWidth, int availableHeight, RenderContext context)
      Description copied from interface: Element
      Returns the preferred size of this element.

      The availableWidth/Height parameters allow elements to adapt their dimensions based on constraints. Use -1 for unconstrained.

      Common patterns:

      • Text elements: height depends on width (text wrapping)
      • Aspect-ratio elements: both dimensions interrelated
      • Fixed elements: ignore available dimensions

      Return value semantics:

      • Positive values = known size (use as constraint)
      • Zero = explicitly zero-sized (element should collapse)
      • Negative (-1) = unknown size (element should fill available space)
      Parameters:
      availableWidth - the available width in cells, or -1 if unconstrained
      availableHeight - the available height in cells, or -1 if unconstrained
      context - the render context for CSS resolution, may be null
      Returns:
      the preferred size

    • styleAttributes

      public Map<String,String> styleAttributes()
      Description copied from interface: Styleable
      Returns the style attributes for attribute selector matching.

      Attribute selectors like Panel[title="Test"] match elements based on their style attributes. This method returns a map of attribute names to their values.

      Common attributes include:

      • title - the element's title
      • label - the element's label
      • placeholder - the element's placeholder text
      Specified by:
      styleAttributes in interface Styleable
      Overrides:
      styleAttributes in class StyledElement<ListElement<T>>
      Returns:
      an unmodifiable map of attribute names to values (never null, may be empty)
